policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וְלַגֵּאָיִוֹת and ketiv ולגאית differ only in plene vs defective spelling of the same plural noun; both read 'and to the valleys'. ASV 6:3 'and to the valleys' renders either identically, and the only note on the verse is an alternative_rendering ('Or, ravines') about the English word choice, not the Hebrew text. Nothing in the ASV distinguishes the readings.
